question: Will a blue LED on 5 V with a 47 ohm resistor fry?
headline: The LED fries: 36.9 mA through it, above its 30 mA rating (1.2x).

checks.name: hand calculation
checks.summary: diode equation solved by hand gives 36.9 mA, ngspice 36.9 mA (5.4e-05% apart); the quick estimate (Vs - Vf)/R is 38.3 mA

checks.name: power balance
checks.summary: supply gives 184 mW = resistor 63.9 mW + LED 120 mW (5.4e-08% apart)

checks.name: operating limits
checks.summary: LED 36.9 mA of 30 mA; resistor 63.9 mW of 250 mW

assumptions: blue LED modeled with the diode equation: 3.2 V at 20 mA, ideality 2.7, series resistance 1.5 ohm.

fixes.title: Use a 91 ohm resistor
fixes.summary: Gives about 19.8 mA; it dissipates 35.6 mW, so a 0.25 W part is enough.
